geometry: Original authored cut-stone lantern assemblies with eight-sided bevelled plinth, waist, shaft, capital, chamber framing, stone umbrella cap and turned finial. Carved wooden hanging lantern masks, recessed individual paper sheets, independent bronze/brass fittings, smooth entasis columns and hollow metal shoes are actual geometry.

wood.use: Existing project albedo, OpenGL normal and roughness maps with member-aligned metric UVs baked into scale buckets. Exposed lacquer colors are material albedo gains.

stone.author: Kless Gyzen
stone.use: Existing scanned geometry retains uniform aspect ratio and original UVs at the two largest lantern foundations. A matching material-space crop [1696,768,544,544] of the actual albedo/normal/roughness atlas is resampled to 512px for authored cut-stone surfaces; albedo is neutralized to gray. The original provider is not claimed to have scanned a temple lantern.

paper: Original mathematical paper-fiber base color and lamp-centered emissive attenuation, on independent inset paper sheets; no view or scene colors sampled.
lighting: Independent local inverse-square point-light pools at lamp centers and a narrowed shrine spotlight. A new actual hanging lamp and connected continuation beam behind the observer replace the old unsupported foreground wash point; no scene-photo lighting or background.
limitations: Interpretive physical construction and material reuse. Actual rendering and visual review are required; this is not a historical survey or photographic acceptance.
